reviewed_by: Claude Code, at the operator's request: stop the provider routing loop from rewording commands a project hook keeps denying
reason: Live Core logged 844 native hook denials across 326 provider turns, up to 16 in one turn: the search-routing hook blocks shell find/grep/tree and the model rewords the command, while every call that runs resets the routing deviation count. A hook manifest can now declare route_to tool names; the denial names them (problem, next_action, use_instead), and without route_to the text is unchanged. The routing loop counts completed denials per hook per turn (serial and parallel waves) and the third denial by the same hook ends routing through the existing deviation-limit path. Selected: the new focused tests, the routing/tolerance and tool-loop suites, the native hook and automation broker suites (the fixture hook now declares route_to), chat, and every tests/v3 file matching _ROUTING_DEVIATION_LIMIT, deviation or NativeHook.
exclusions: No UI or settings change, so no frontend, Playwright or LAN Core run. 22 selected tests fail identically on pristine origin/main (verified by running them against an origin/main export): test_chat.py::test_runtime_switch_to_equal_limits_needs_no_confirmation_over_target[postgresql], 4 in test_automation_runtime.py (host mode and network scope) and 17 in test_universal_agent_tools.py (un-awaited coroutine rot).
